question_stem: Existing RLHF and DPO both rely on a preference model like Bradley-Terry. According to the introduction, how does DPO use that model differently to remove two parts of the standard pipeline?
The optimal policy expression contains an intractable partition function $Z(x)$. How does DPO get rid of it when moving from rewards to preference probabilities?
How do the coding-assistant and misconception examples support the paper’s claim that alignment is about selecting behavior from capabilities rather than adding knowledge?
Why is the KL term in the standard RLHF objective described as doing more than just regularization?

In the related-work discussion outside language, what two properties distinguish DPO’s target setting from contextual dueling bandits and standard preference-based RL, and how do those differences motivate DPO’s single-stage approach?
When training from an existing preference dataset, why do the authors care so much about how $\pi_\text{ref}$ is chosen?
In the actor-critic analysis, why is the normalization term practically important even though it does not change the optimum, and why does DPO not need extra baselines for it?
Why is Best-of-N included as a baseline if the paper argues for simpler training methods?
Why do the authors switch from exact reward/KL evaluation in sentiment to GPT-4 win rates in summarization and dialogue, and what evidence do they provide that this switch is reasonable?
What exact normalization condition can DPO be seen as imposing on each reward equivalence class, and why is that useful?
How do the equivalence-class lemmas support the claim that DPO’s reward reparameterization does not lose generality?
What combination of results in summarization suggests DPO’s gains are not just a lucky decoding-temperature choice?
Why do the CNN/DailyMail results count as nontrivial evidence for DPO’s generalization ability relative to PPO?
Which two open problems in the discussion tie together model behavior and evaluation, rather than just scale?
Why did the authors introduce the GPT-4 (C) evaluation prompt, and why did they use it for the main reported results?
In the dialogue experiments, why do the authors first build a reference model with Preferred-FT, and what do the resulting comparisons imply about DPO?
